title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 14
paragraphs: So when the Phoenicians sailed to the attack, the Ionians put out their ships from shore against them, sailing in single file. When they came near and engaged one another in battle, as for what followed I am not able to record precisely which of the Ionians showed themselves cowards or brave men in this sea-fight, for they throw blame on one another. The Samians, however, it is said, in accordance with their agreement with Aeaces, put up their sails and set off from their station in the line to sail back to Samos—except for eleven ships: the captains of these stayed in their places and took part in the sea-fight, refusing to obey their division commanders. The Samian state granted them, for this reason, to have their names inscribed on a pillar together with their fathers' names, as having proved themselves brave men; and this pillar still exists in the marketplace. Then the Lesbians, too, when they saw those next them in the line taking to flight, did the same as the Samians; and most of the Ionians also did the very same thing.
